I've been working this land in Quzhou for four decades. My wheat and maize rotate on the same plots — that's how we do it here, has been since before my father. The millet I keep on the poorer, sandier ground to the east of my plots, maybe 5 or 6 mu worth. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves now that the children are in the city. During wheat harvest and maize planting rush, my son comes back to help.

**My thinking, crop by crop:**

**Wheat (winter):** I'll sow about 15 mu come October, same plots as always. I use Jimai 22 — it's proven here, my neighbors use it, the seed shop stocks it. I apply diammonium phosphate and urea as base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing in March. I irrigate four times: the winter water before freeze, then jointing, heading, and grain fill. We had stripe rust two years ago so I'll spray once more this year for fungicide. Rotary till after maize harvest to prepare the seedbed.

**Maize (summer):** Same 15 mu, right after wheat harvest in June. I buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed from the township supply co-op. For fertilizer I apply a compound base and then chase it with urea when the plants are knee-high. I've been direct-seeding into the wheat stubble the last few years — saves time, keeps moisture. Three irrigations: at establishment, tasseling, and filling. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide first, then borer control.

**Millet (spring):** My 5.4 mu of millet I sow in May. I keep a local improved variety I've saved seed from for years. Less fertilizer needed, less water. Two irrigations from my well. I rarely need more than one spray for weeds.
